subject: Re: 🔵{Brand} & MobUpps
body:
Hi RECIPIENT_NAME,
Following up on my earlier email about win-back for your dormant orderers. Here is the fresh angle worth your time: Food and Drink day-30 retention sits between 3.7% and 3.9%, so almost every fresh install lapses inside the first month and fresh UA keeps refilling a leaky bucket. That is why DoorDash and Uber Eats lean hard on reactivation. Re-engaging an already-validated dormant orderer is the cheaper order, and we hold out a control group so recovered orders read as incremental to your habitual reorderers. Worth comparing to your current source mix?
angle: fresh angle: leaky-bucket UA economics + Food & Drink day-30 retention 3.7-3.9% band (sourced)
register_notes: Stage 2 EN US food_and_delivery: acknowledges second follow-up and references prior email in first sentence; fresh angle = leaky-bucket UA economics anchored to web-verified Food & Drink day-30 retention band 3.7-3.9% (growth-onomics, carried verbatim from parent verified sources); no MobUpps figure this stage; MobUpps holdout/incrementality referenced without a number; exactly 1 question mark; peers reused from parent named set (DoorDash, Uber Eats) only, no out-of-set or sister-brand pairing; native register; no sign-off; no em dash; no X-not-Y.
